cells.verb: choosing one real connection and letting yourself join it
cells.place: at the point where nothing has been decided yet
cells.ask: This balance is free to feed something next: when something easier offers itself this week, stay with the one you chose, and let the staying come from how it feels rather than from a rule. What comes back is direction that moves because you're actually in it.
cells.core: You're letting something real form while everything is still open. Not closing every door and not keeping them all cracked — one connection is getting your yes, and the yes is coming from somewhere true in you, while the rest of the field stays wide. That's harder than it looks: most people either grab or hold off. You're joining one current without losing the sky.
cells.sheetLine: You're saying yes to one thing while the rest stays open, and the yes is yours.

cells.tense: Future — bracing at a page that isn't written yet
cells.verb: rushing to join before there's anything to join
cells.place: at the point where nothing has been decided yet
cells.ask: The medicine isn't to choose better. It's to tend one thing without deciding what it becomes — water it, show up for it, and leave the shape of it unsettled for a while. What comes back is a vision that arrives because you've actually lived the thing, not because you needed the open field to close.
cells.core: You're merging with something to get out of the openness. Nothing's been decided yet, and that undecided stretch ahead feels unbearable, so you keep reaching for a connection and pouring yourself in before it's had time to be anything. The joining is real; the timing isn't yours. You're choosing the current so you don't have to stand in the open.
cells.sheetLine: You're joining fast so you won't have to stand in the open.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you
cells.verb: keeping every connection possible so none of them has to be real
cells.place: at the point where nothing has been decided yet
cells.ask: The way back isn't to force a yes. It's to let yourself know more — notice which pull is actually true for you, without deciding anything about it, and let that knowing sit even when it's incomplete. What comes back is a vision that flows because something has finally been let all the way in.
cells.core: You're holding the field open so nothing has to become anything. Somewhere back there, joining with something meant losing the rest, and you've kept the whole sky available ever since. But everything-possible has started to mean nothing-chosen, and the current you could have joined is running without you. The openness is still there. The choosing stopped.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping everything possible so you never have to join anything.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing
cells.verb: already flowing with one connection while calling it undecided
cells.place: at the point where nothing has been decided yet
cells.ask: The medicine is simpler than it sounds: say out loud, to one person, where you're already headed — as a direction, not a question. Show someone the way you're already walking. What comes back is a vision you can stand behind, because it's finally coming from what you've actually chosen.
cells.core: You've already joined something. People can see it in where your attention goes, what you make time for, what you can't stop returning to — you're in the current and you've been in it a while. But you'd say you're still weighing options. The connection has been chosen. The naming of it hasn't happened, and the openness you're protecting is already gone.
cells.sheetLine: You've already chosen the connection. You're still calling the field open.
